map.filter_min_frequency_help: Minimum occurrences for a node: documents with the term or author, or cocitations of a reference. This does not set how many nodes appear; use Max. Nodes below.
map.filter_max_nodes_help: Shows up to 100 terms in co-occurrence or 100 authors in co-authorship by default. Enter another number to change the limit. Zero shows all eligible nodes. When Top % is set, it overrides this limit.
map.filter_top_percent_help: For co-occurrence and co-authorship, shows only the entered percentage of the most relevant nodes. When set, it overrides Max. Nodes.

strings_base.nota.curinga_removido: wildcard (*) removed — this source has no prefix expansion
strings_base.nota.virgula_removida: comma removed — it would break the query
strings_base.nota.negacao_descartada: NOT dropped: this source cannot exclude
strings_base.nota.sem_booleano: no booleans: this source ranks by relevance
strings_base.nota.termos_cortados: terms beyond the twelfth were cut
busca_ia.regras: The string MUST contain ONLY topical terms, the operators AND, OR and NOT in uppercase, double quotes for phrases and parentheses for grouping. FORBIDDEN: wildcards/asterisks (spell the variants out with OR: (bibliometric OR bibliometrics)), commas, field tags such as [tiab] or [MeSH], and syntax from other databases such as TITLE-ABS-KEY(), TS= or AB=. Do NOT put year, language, document type or open access inside the string: Blicsa has its own filters for that — tell the user to use the on-screen fields. Give ONE string only, inside a code block, on the last line of your answer; Blicsa translates it to OpenAlex, Crossref and PubMed on its own.
busca_ia.prompt_sem_string: I need to build a bibliometric search string. Explain the operators and how to pick the terms, and finish by proposing an example string. {regras}
busca_ia.prompt_com_string: Review the search string I configured: what it gets right, what it misses and what it over-excludes. Finish by proposing a new, better string. {regras}
busca_ia.bolha_sem_string: Help me build a search string.

relatorio.decl_sem_ia: No artificial intelligence tool was used in this research.
relatorio.decl_abertura: This research used the language model {modelos} (via {provedores}), accessed through the Blicsa software {versao}, in {chamadas} recorded calls.
relatorio.decl_interpreta: In {n} the model's output was incorporated into the result ({pontos}).
relatorio.decl_descreve: In {n} of them the model produced interpretive text about the results, presented as AI-generated content and labelled as such in the interface.
relatorio.decl_aconselha: In {n} of them the model was consulted to support methodological decisions — formulating the search strategy and preliminary reading of results — without its output entering the data.
relatorio.decl_responsabilidade: Collection, processing and bibliometric analyses were carried out by the software's deterministic algorithms, without model involvement. Final interpretation and writing are the responsibility of the authors, who reviewed all generated content.
relatorio.sem_medida: Calls with no token count from the provider, excluded from the totals above: {n}.
relatorio.falhas: Calls that failed, recorded as attempts: {n}.
relatorio.sem_buscas: No search recorded in this project.
